about.title: Ceres Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Ceres sees its share of crashes along the corridors that carry most of its daily traffic — Mitchell Road, Hatch Road, and both stretches of Whitmore Avenue. Public records show 201 injury collisions and 281 injured people in the most recent final year, with Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. drawing the heaviest reports. Whether you were stopped at a light near Whitmore Avenue or sideswiped merging onto Hatch Road, the days right after a crash matter. Insurance adjusters move fast, and evidence like skid marks, dashcam footage, or witness memory fades quickly. We help injured Ceres residents evaluate the crash, protect what evidence remains, and handle communication with insurers while you focus on recovery. There's no obligation and no upfront cost to get started.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Talking to the Insurer

items.title: California's Clock Is Already Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury claim, but if a government vehicle or road defect was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. We can help identify which deadline applies to your situation.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Cut Your Recovery
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning your compensation can be reduced by whatever percentage of blame the insurer assigns to you. A recorded statement given too soon, before facts are clear, can be used to inflate that percentage against you.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages, No Upfront Cost
items.desc: California places no cap on damages for pain, suffering, and other non-economic losses in most car accident cases. We work on contingency, so there's no fee unless you recover.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to shift fault or minimize your claim later. We can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a Ceres crash?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of the accident to file a personal injury lawsuit. That window can be much shorter, sometimes just six months, if a city or county vehicle or roadway was involved, such as a crash near a public intersection on Whitmore Avenue. We can confirm which deadline applies to your case.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault, so you can still recover compensation even if you share some responsibility for the crash. Your recovery is simply reduced by your percentage of fault. This is one reason it helps to have us review the details before the insurer assigns blame.

items.question: Is there a charge for your services?
items.answer: No. We provide a free consultation, and if we take your case, we typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
